items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Monsieur Georges had telephoned the steamship officials in Villefranche and arranged the difficult task of postponing the sailing time of the crack Italian liner one hour in order for us to get aboard.

ctx.x: When we arrived in Nice, I saw all the heavy baggage we were carrying still at the station. I thought something was funny because the baggage had come on the train which the others had taken. From Nice we had to go to Villefranche to board the Italian steamer REX which was the largest ship plying the Atlantic and was the holder of the Blue Riband for being the fastest ocean liner in the world.

The Rex was supposed to sail from Villefranche at the same time our train arrived in Nice but Monsieur Georges had telephoned the steamship officials in Villefranche and arranged the difficult task of postponing the sailing time of the crack Italian liner one hour in order for us to get aboard.

A launch was waiting to take us out to the Rex. There was no landing port in Villefranche for large steamers, so the passengers were put ashore or taken out to the ships in launches. Most of the passengers on board knew that the ship was delayed from sailing because two passengers were arriving late so the decks were lined with passengers, curious to see who these two persons could be. And they really did wave and cheer us when we were climbing up the steps to the boarding deck.
